feature: HTTP/2 WebTransport listener request and connection lookup deadlines

behavior.lookup: all listener Session operations pass the original deadline through connection-table mutex admission and then to the EndpointServer command; cancellation is checked before retaining the connection
behavior.request: request dequeue uses deadline-aware mutex admission and checks cancellation before consuming ready metadata; expired/canceled attempts leave the first owned queued request intact
behavior.reacquisition: after an event wake the receiver reacquires State with the original deadline, without renewing the budget or using an uncancellable mutex wait
behavior.lifetime: receive retains State before entering the wait and transfers that reference to a delivered PendingRequest; failed lookup/receive releases it without relocking State
behavior.shutdown: close publishes closed before queue draining; each queued request is taken under the mutex and released outside it, allowing registered receivers to observe ListenerClosed without racing destruction or queue cleanup

regressions: 16 public listener operations under a held State mutex return Timeout or Canceled with unchanged queue/connection state and parent references; expired or wrong-clock inputs never enter lock wait
a request receiver is woken while its second mutex acquisition is held, then returns Timeout under the original budget and releases its State reference without reacquiring the mutex for cleanup
close with a parked request receiver retains State until that receiver returns ListenerClosed

the real two-connection TLS listener has an already ready request queue; expired and canceled calls preserve the first queue entry, which later valid callers accept and exchange independent Session traffic
independent Python TLS client negotiates a Session through actual EndpointListener, sends fragmented stream and DATAGRAM, receives exact stream reply/DATAGRAM and CLOSE code 19

limitations: concurrent owner close requires the operation to have entered before the owning handle is destroyed; retaining inside an already-entered operation does not authorize starting calls from a destroyed handle
listener connection reservation/publication and shutdown pacing have distinct owner lifecycle boundaries beyond this facade lookup/dequeue capture
broader protocol integration and multi-hour/high-concurrency evidence remain open for the overall goal
